answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Binding. Each identity must answer a random challenge whose correct response depends on its private history, so clones that share a template cannot answer differently and are caught. An island of independent agents keeps distinct records; any fable of uniqueness collapses when two clones return identical answers. A mirror check compares challenge responses across identities. Cost: the attacker must maintain and differentiate every clone’s history, paying full per-identity computation and storage rather than copying one payload.
